description: Run the four mandatory pre-coding reference captures (PC1/PC2/PC3/PC-SYS) that pin the externally-defined Solana contract facts the authoritative sources describe only semantically, and record the measured results into design.md (§2.1 opcode delta, §4.3 R_BPF numeric table + lddw split, §4.4 DSO layout contract, §7 PC-SYS syscall decision). These are READ-ONLY inspections of a cargo build-sbf reference .so run under WSL with the Solana toolchain; the Solana toolchain is never part of the Sig artifact path. This feature gates all coding features (FEAT-002..005) because the recorded tables are the authority FEAT-003/004 implement against. No Sig source is modified in this feature.
steps: Set up a WSL working dir and build a trivial Rust Solana program whose entrypoint logs and returns 0 using `cargo build-sbf` (Solana toolchain). Keep the output .so as the reference artifact. Record the toolchain versions used.

PC1 (pins A1, design §2.1): `llvm-objdump -d` the reference .so to list its opcodes; build the equivalent trivial `.sig` entrypoint (export fn entrypoint(input: [*]u8) callconv(.c) u64) with the stage0 sig at C:\Just-Things\Projects\Lib\sig-latest\bin\sig.exe via `sig build-obj -target bpfel -mcpu v3`, disassemble it, and diff the opcode multisets. Record the delta table in design.md §2.1. If non-empty, apply the §2.1 fallback ladder; if an sBPFv3-only opcode is unreachable without a forked LLVM backend, STOP and escalate via send_message severity warning (do not proceed to coding).

PC2 (pins A5, design §4.3): `llvm-readelf -r` the reference .so; record the exact numeric R_BPF_* relocation values actually used and, for one lddw-based relocation, the two-slot immediate bit layout (which 32 bits land in the first vs the following instruction slot). Overwrite design.md §4.3's expected table with the measured values.

PC3 (pins A6, design §4.4; design-review NIT 2): `llvm-readelf -a` the reference .so; record e_type, e_machine, class/endianness, the PT_LOAD set + flags + p_align vs whether the loader consumes section headers only, the section set present (.text/.rodata/.dynamic/.dynsym/.dynstr/.rel(a).dyn and whether .data.rel.ro is folded), DT_REL vs DT_RELA, whether a .hash/.gnu.hash section is present and whether the loader tolerates it, and the entrypoint dynamic-symbol attributes (name/binding/type/visibility). Overwrite design.md §4.4's expected contract.

PC-SYS (resolves A9, design §7): inspect src/codegen/llvm.sig extern/call handling (around genNavRef, lines ~487/793/869/1017), and emit a one-line test that calls a no-library `extern fn sol_log_(...) callconv(.c)`; `llvm-objdump -d` the object to see whether the vendored LLVM BPF backend renders it as `call <imm>` or a symbol-relocated call. Confirm murmur3-32 of a known syscall name (e.g. sol_log_) matches the immediate in the reference .so's call (nail the seed/name encoding). Record in design.md §7 whether the committed codegen `call imm` path is physically possible or the linker-side R_BPF_SYSCALL fallback is required.
Save all capture logs (objdump/readelf outputs) under .build/sbpf-test/refcap/ in the worktree for traceability. Commit the design.md updates on branch feat/sbpf-solana.
acceptance_criteria: design.md §4.3 contains concrete measured R_BPF_* numeric values (not the word 'expected') and the measured lddw immediate split.
design.md §4.4 contains the measured DSO layout contract: e_type, DT_REL/DT_RELA, segment/section set, p_align, hash-section presence/tolerance, entrypoint dynsym attributes.
design.md §2.1 records the PC1 opcode delta (expected empty); if non-empty the §2.1 fallback/escalation path is recorded.
design.md §7 records the PC-SYS decision (codegen call-imm path vs linker R_BPF_SYSCALL fallback) with the confirmed murmur3-32 seed/encoding.
verification: Open design.md and confirm §2.1, §4.3, §4.4, §7 are filled with measured values rather than 'expected'/'to be confirmed' placeholders.
Confirm .build/sbpf-test/refcap/ contains the llvm-objdump and llvm-readelf outputs the captures were read from.
findings:
All four pre-coding reference captures ran under WSL (Ubuntu) with the Solana toolchain installed read-only: cargo-build-sbf 4.4.0 / platform-tools v1.57 (LLVM 22.1.2-rust-dev), solana-cli 4.3.0, rustc 1.95 (sbf). Reference artifact: a trivial Rust entrypoint!/msg! program built for sbpfv3-solana-solana. Sig side: stage0 sig 0.6.0 (zig 0.17.0). Logs in .build/sbpf-test/refcap/. Design updates recorded in design.md Measured-result blocks for 2.1/4.3/4.4/7.

PC2 — R_SBF relocation values (MEASURED, override the design's prior 'expected' guesses): the symbols are named R_SBF_* (not R_BPF_*). Only three types appear in a real sBPFv3 relocatable object: R_SBF_64_64 = 1 (0x01), R_SBF_64_ABS64 = 2 (0x02), R_SBF_64_32 = 10 (0x0a, the dominant/call-and-32-bit-ref type). There is NO R_SBF_64_ABS32 and NO R_SBF_64_RELATIVE; the 32-bit case is type 10, not 3; do not use upstream-eBPF numbering. Relocation sections are .rel.* = SHT_REL, entry size 0x10 (8-byte r_offset + 8-byte r_info, NO explicit addend) => REL form with implicit addends. lddw split (R_SBF_64_64): the 64-bit immediate is split across two 8-byte instruction slots' imm fields (bytes [4..8) little-endian) — LOW 32 bits in slot 1's imm, HIGH 32 bits in slot 2's imm (verified: 18 03 00 00 00 00 00 00 / 00 00 00 00 03 00 00 00 => lddw r3, 0x300000000). First slot opcode byte is 0x18.

PC3 — DSO layout + DT_REL/DT_RELA decision (MEASURED): e_type=ET_DYN, e_machine=EM_BPF(247), ELFCLASS64, little-endian, e_flags=0x3. The loader enters via e_entry (0x100000308 in the reference), NOT a dynamic-symbol lookup. The final sBPFv3 deploy artifact is static and relocation-free: only four sections (NULL, .rodata [WAMS, addr 0x0, align 8], .text [AX, addr 0x100000000, align 8], .shstrtab) — NO .dynamic, NO .dynsym/.dynstr, NO .hash/.gnu.hash, NO .plt/.got, and 'no relocations in this file' (all R_SBF_* resolved at link time). .data.rel.ro is folded into .rodata. 3 program headers: LOAD(R, off 0xe8, vaddr 0x0, p_align 0x8) for rodata; LOAD(E, off 0x570, vaddr 0x100000000, p_align 0x8) for text; NULL terminator. DECISION: targetPageAlign for BPF must be 0x8 (NOT 0x1000 — correct the design 4.2a arm). DT_REL vs DT_RELA is MOOT for the final artifact (no .dynamic/dyn-reloc table); at the relocatable-object level the form is REL (SHT_REL, implicit addends), so the linker reads REL input relocs and resolves them into section contents, emitting no dynamic reloc table on output. Entrypoint dynsym attributes: symbol name 'entrypoint', binding GLOBAL, type FUNC, visibility DEFAULT, in .text, value == e_entry — a STATIC .symtab symbol, not a dynamic one.

PC-SYS — syscall-lowering path (RESOLVES A9): CODEGEN call-imm path, NOT a linker R_SBF/R_BPF_SYSCALL fallback. The reference uses two call forms off opcode 0x85: '85 10 00 00 <rel32>' (src reg 1) = PC-relative internal call; '85 00 00 00 <imm32>' (src reg 0) = static syscall with a fixed hashed immediate and NO relocation. murmur3 seed/encoding CONFIRMED bit-exact: MurmurHash3_x86_32, seed=0, hashing the raw ASCII syscall name, imm32 = the hash. Measured matches: sol_log_ => 0x207559bd; sol_memcpy_ => 0x717cc4a3; abort => 0xb6fc1a11 (shown by objdump as call -0x4903e5ef). FEAT-004 implements this in src/codegen/llvm.sig (recognize no-lib extern fn callconv(.c) under os.tag==.solana as a static syscall, emit call imm with imm=murmur3_32(name,0), src reg 0, no reloc). The data relocations (R_SBF_64_64/64_ABS64/64_32) are still needed for address/data refs; PC-SYS only settles the syscall-call mechanism.

PC1 — opcode delta (A1 HOLDS, no escalation): the Sig trivial entrypoint lowers to exactly b7 mov64 r0,0x0 + 95 exit, a strict subset of the reference. The reference .so uses 48 distinct opcodes, ALL decoded cleanly by llvm-objdump --mcpu=v3 (zero <unknown>/.byte/invalid) — ordinary eBPF v1-v3 ISA (mov/ldx/stx/alu/jumps/call/callx/lddw/be64, signed jumps, 32-bit store-imm). Opcode delta that stock bpfel -mcpu v3 cannot emit: EMPTY. The Solana platform-tools backend is a fork of the same LLVM 22 BPF backend, so no sBPFv3-only opcode is required or unreachable. The 2.1 fallback ladder is not triggered; the 'reuse .bpfel arch unchanged' decision (3.1) stands. The sBPFv3 contract difference is entirely in linking/syscall-encoding/layout (PC2/PC3/PC-SYS), not the instruction set.
